title: Profile manifest transformation and runner fallback for onboarding
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Introduce a declarative transformation layer that normalizes profile manifests emitted by the benchmark harness and provides a graceful fallback shim for legacy eval runners. This ticket covers: (1) dataset contract normalization (column names, expected fields, label schemes); (2) deterministic prompt-variant hashing and canonicalization so profiles are stable across runner implementations; (3) a lightweight runner-fallback shim that can execute profiles against older eval runners without requiring full harness refactors; and (4) integration hooks to publish the final performance profile to the profile registry and console job artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Profile manifests produced by the harness are normalized to the canonical schema v2 and pass the manifest-validator with zero warnings
Prompt variants include stable hashing and seed metadata such that the same logical variant maps to the same profile id across runs
Runner-fallback shim can execute 90% of our common eval runner contracts (TorchRunner, LegacyGoRunner) with <=5% overhead
Published profiles appear in profile-registry with correct metadata (model_version, dataset_signature, rollout_tags) and console shows per-route token cost delta
End-to-end pipeline covered by an automated integration test that runs on CI with a small sample dataset and asserts profile id determinism

2026-03-09: Integration test added to CI (pipeline: ci/profile-publish-smoke). Flaky case found when dataset uses 'expected_output' vs 'label' field — added normalization rule to schema v2.

technical_notes: Manifest schema v2 flattens dataset descriptors and adds canonical_field_names mapping to accommodate legacy CSVs and JSONL
Prompt-variant hashing uses 'sha1(model_name + canonical_prompt + seed + dataset_signature)'; storing first 8 chars as profile_short_id
The runner-fallback shim wraps legacy runner APIs and maps new harness hooks to legacy call signatures; configured via feature-flag and runtime adapter registry
KV cache compatibility: profile publishing will include kv_cache_fingerprint to enable reuse between model variants where possible
We add a manifest version field and keep transformation logic idempotent so re-running transformation on v2 outputs leaves them unchanged
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest transformations (edge cases: missing label, multi-turn prompts, function-calling outputs)
Integration CI job runs harness with 'profile_shim_v1' enabled against small-sample datasets and verifies published profile ids match golden manifests
Performance benchmark measuring runner-fallback overhead across 3 runner implementations with at least 1000 tokens total
Manual QA: run onboarding flow with 3 internal models and confirm profiles appear in console and can be pinned to rollout rules
estimated_cost_saving: ~12-18% token-cost reduction for repeat-inference workloads via canonicalization and KV cache reuse
